overall: The AG found the Stoughton School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law; the June 7 executive session minutes substantially complied with the accuracy and detail requirement. Complaint resolved.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the June 7 executive session minutes omitted his request to record the session.
allegations.key_passage: First, although the minutes fail to reflect the complainant's request to record the executive session, such a statement is not required to be recorded in the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the June 7 executive session minutes omitted certain comments made by the Committee chair.
allegations.key_passage: Second, we find that the minutes reflect comments made by the chair and the reason the Committee took two votes to amend and approve the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the minutes did not explain why the Committee took two separate roll call votes to approve the amended executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Second, we find that the minutes reflect comments made by the chair and the reason the Committee took two votes to amend and approve the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the minutes inaccurately summarized his comment that the first element of his complaint was satisfied but not the second.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, the portion of the minutes concerning the complainant's comments about elements of his complaints being satisfied, while not verbatim, sufficiently summarizes his comments.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
